title: The OSI and TCP/IP Models: How Layers Organize a Network

questions.question: How many layers does the OSI reference model define?
questions.rationale: OSI defines seven layers: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data link, Physical.

questions.question: Which OSI layer handles logical addressing and routing between networks?
questions.rationale: Layer 3, the Network layer, does logical addressing and routing — its examples are IP, ICMP, and routers.

questions.question: What is the protocol data unit (PDU) at the data link layer?
questions.rationale: Layer 2 delivers frames over one hop; layer 1 carries bits, layer 3 packets, and layer 4 segments.

questions.question: In the bottom-up mnemonic Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away, which layer does Throw stand for?
questions.rationale: Reading bottom-up the words map Physical, Data link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application — so Throw is Transport.

questions.question: The TCP/IP model has how many layers?
questions.rationale: TCP/IP compresses OSI into four layers: Application, Transport, Internet, and Link.

questions.question: The TCP/IP Application layer corresponds to which OSI layers?
questions.rationale: The mapping table shows TCP/IP Application covering OSI Application, Presentation, and Session — everything user-facing.

questions.question: Encapsulation on the way down the stack means:
options: Each layer treats the layer above's data as an opaque payload and adds its own header
Data is encrypted at every layer
Headers are only added at layer 1
questions.rationale: Sending wraps the message layer by layer — data becomes a segment with a TCP header, a packet with an IP header, then a frame — each layer treating the payload as opaque.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the TCP three-way handshake?
questions.rationale: The client sends SYN, the server answers SYN-ACK, and the client returns ACK — after which the connection is open.

questions.question: Why does a live voice call prefer UDP over TCP?
options: It would rather skip a lost syllable than pause the conversation to request it again
questions.rationale: TCP's ACKs and retransmission add delay; for live audio a small gap beats a stalled conversation, which is why VoIP uses UDP.

questions.question: How do the TCP and UDP header sizes compare?
questions.rationale: The comparison table lists TCP headers at 20 bytes and UDP headers at 8 bytes — one reason UDP is faster with minimal overhead.
